corrections.workload: Microbenchmarks on tiny fixed string sets, timed as totals with CLOCK_MONOTONIC: grapheme counting over 8 short strings x 200,000 iterations (bench_grapheme.c; ICU ubrk UBRK_CHARACTER iterator reused via ubrk_setText); NFC normalization of 10 short strings x 100,000 (bench_nfc.c; ICU unorm2_normalize into UTF-16); NFC quick-check of 9 already-NFC strings x 500,000 (bench_nfc_quickcheck.c; ICU u_strFromUTF8 plus unorm2_isNormalized); three-level comparison of 12 string pairs x 100,000 (bench_collate.c; ICU ucol_strcoll with ucol_open(""), i.e. CLDR root collation). The 'UTF-8 input' scenario times ICU including u_strFromUTF8 conversion; the 'core-to-core' scenario feeds ICU pre-converted UTF-16.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (M5 Max, ICU 78.3), UTF-8 input with ICU paying u_strFromUTF8 conversion: NFC 28 ms vs 59 ms (2.1x), NFC quick-check 62 ms vs 237 ms (3.8x), collation 31 ms vs 40 ms (1.3x), grapheme segmentation 237 ms vs 337 ms (1.4x). Core-to-core (ICU on pre-converted UTF-16): NFC 28 ms vs 39 ms (libutf 1.4x), grapheme 237 ms vs 277 ms (libutf 1.2x), collation 31 ms vs 22 ms (ICU 1.4x faster). No core-to-core figure exists for quick-check. Numbers predate later correctness fixes to the grapheme, NFC and collation code.
corrections.caveats: First-party microbenchmark on 8 to 12 short hand-written strings repeated 100,000 to 500,000 times, so it measures per-call overhead, not bulk throughput; README reports totals only and no raw result files are checked in. The README numbers were refreshed on 2026-07-30, before correctness fixes to grapheme segmentation (GB4 after CR, GB11 single ZWJ, GB12/13 adjacent regional indicators, 2026-09-29), NFC (D115 blocked composition, 2026-08-01) and collation (NFC tiebreak buffer sizing, 2026-09-04); they have not been re-measured. Grapheme segmentation is not equivalent work: src/grapheme.c implements Unicode 16.0 rules GB3-GB13 without GB9c (Indic conjunct breaks, in UAX #29 since Unicode 15.1), so on the benchmark's Devanagari string it returns a different cluster count from ICU, which follows Unicode 17 in ICU 78.x; there is no GraphemeBreakTest conformance test in tests/ (only test_color_ops.c, test_nfc_icu.c, test_collate_icu.c). Unicode versions differ for all modules (libutf 16.0, ICU 78 is 17.0). The 'UTF-8 input' headline ratios charge ICU for u_strFromUTF8 even though ICU offers native UTF-8 paths that the benchmark does not use (ucol_strcollUTF8, UText via utext_openUTF8 with ubrk_setUText, C++ Normalizer2::normalizeUTF8 and isNormalizedUTF8); core-to-core the gaps shrink to 1.2x to 1.4x and ICU wins collation by 1.4x. ICU's collator is CLDR root collation (ucol_open("")), not raw DUCET. Compiler version and ICU 78.3 build configuration are not stated. NFC and collation are differentially tested against ICU (50 NFC cases plus a 100,000-input fuzz, 33 collation comparisons). Category fit: Unicode segmentation, normalization and collation (ICU baseline), not font shaping; HarfBuzz and FreeType do not apply.

notes: Downgraded A to C: harness is public and readable, but the published numbers predate correctness fixes to every benchmarked module, and the grapheme path skips GB9c and targets Unicode 16 against ICU's Unicode 17. NFC core-to-core 1.4x is the most like-for-like number (differentially tested against ICU). Category for the orchestrator: this is Unicode segmentation/normalization/collation and belongs in wave 3's unicode-utf8 category with the ICU baseline, not font-shaping-text-layout.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark with no benchmark code in the repo; compiler, flags and the msdfgen version (2019 era) are not stated. GPU versus CPU: the msdfgl timings run on the laptop's integrated Intel UHD Graphics 620 and the msdfgen timings on the same laptop's 4-core CPU (README writes 'Core i7 8550m'), so it is the same SoC rather than a discrete GPU, but the win comes from moving the per-pixel step to the GPU, not from a faster CPU algorithm, and it needs an OpenGL 3.3 or ES 3.2 context. msdfgen's timing excludes uploading the bitmaps to a texture while msdfgl's includes it (favors msdfgen); shader compilation (close to a second) and GL context creation are excluded. The scale 8.0 msdfgen values (8.0000 s and 31.0000 s) are extrapolated, not measured. msdfgl drops cubic segments (README TODO: needed for OpenType/CFF fonts) and lacks edge-coloring for teardrop contours with 1 or 2 segments; the test font DejaVu Sans is TrueType (quadratic only), so the benchmark avoids the missing paths. Output quality parity with msdfgen, including its error correction, is not evaluated. Baseline is msdfgen, not a listed incumbent (HarfBuzz, FreeType). Numbers read from bar labels in img/benchmarks.png.

notes: Confirmed at C; chart labels match the record exactly and the derived ratios check out (0.4890/0.0081 = 60x, 31.0/0.2345 = 132x vs single-threaded; 16x to 34x vs OpenMP).
